name: FDE Trilattice-Derived DQI

phase_0.boundary_condition: The 4-valued Belnap–Dunn lattice BIT_2^3 generated by 2^16 subsets over three independent truth orderings (information, truth, constructivity)

⊢.chosen_element: uninitiated trilattice vertex — the empty set of {T, F, t, f} components prior to any DQI measurement
⊢.justification: Analogous to the seed before a quantum channel is prepared; corresponds to the algebraic initial object that generates the SIXTEEN_3 lattice

⊣.chosen_element: the all-and-only-defined lattice point x* where every base value is simultaneously affirmed and refuted in the three orderings
⊣.justification: Fixed point of the negation in the SIXTEEN_3 bilattice; the constitutional closed boundary that contains the full lattice under all three orderings simultaneously

≻.chosen_element: the truth-ordering forward morphism promoting t* = (T, t) (true and acceptable) by establishing a non-designated DQI success
≻.justification: The directed morphism that advances the channel toward a true/acceptable component reading in the designated t axis, mirroring CL on the T arm

≺.chosen_element: the designated-ordering reverse morphism demoting a false-but-rejectable reading on the F arm of a forked DQI
≺.justification: The contravariant descent that tracks a non-acceptable refutation, mirroring AFWD on the F arm and corresponding to the 'miracle-max' aspect of the DQI

⋈.chosen_element: the sequential composition of DQI channels (a ∘ b), concatenating output state of one into the input of the next
⋈.justification: Aguilera–Baez–Mundici's DQI channel composition is the canonical associative operator on the regular closed-subset lattice; this is the linear glue between operations

⊙.chosen_element: identity DQI channel id(x) = x (a noiseless identity map)
⊙.justification: Self-reference; the identity element of the regular closed-subset monoid; corresponds to the central involution (or G3 element) of the SIXTEEN_3 lattice under classical negation

∈.chosen_element: a DQI-fork (send the same input through two complementary channels producing a T-arm and an F-arm reading)
∈.justification: Represents the genuine either/or of a DQI measurement: two arms carrying the affirmative and the negative evaluation of the input bit

∋.chosen_element: the reunion of the two fork arms back into a single B4 verdict through the Belnap join ⊔
∋.justification: Reconstitutes the fork into a single B4 evaluation; conflicting arms rejoin to B (both); compatible arms rejoin to T or F depending on the input's truth value in the chosen ordering

⊤.chosen_element: affirmative B4 verdict: T — the input is constructively proven true in the designated ordering of the DQI
⊤.justification: The success arm; explicitly designates the positive outcome of the DQI evaluation on the T-side of the fork

⊥.chosen_element: negative B4 verdict: F — the input is constructively refuted false in the designated ordering of the DQI
⊥.justification: The failure arm; explicitly designates the refutation outcome of the DQI evaluation on the F-side of the fork

⊞.chosen_element: paradice B4 verdict: B = (T, F, t, f) with all four base values held simultaneously as the contradiction of the DQI
⊞.justification: The dialetheic state — contradiction kept live without explosion; corresponds to the Aguilera–Baez–Mundici miracle-paradice pair and the FSPLIT/FFUSE rejoin when both arms disagree

⊡.chosen_element: a DQI verdict frozen as a permanent append-only record (an audit log of evaluations that cannot be reversed)
⊡.justification: ROM fixation of a Belnap evaluation; preserves the closed nature of the underlying regular closed-subset structure as a measurement history

phase_2.split_element: DQI-fork of a regular closed input Ω under two complementary measurement channels
phase_2.split_input: Ω — a regular closed subset of the two-point deontic algebra 2 = {0, 1}
split_outputs: channel A giving a T-arm reading (T or t) in the designated ordering
channel B giving an F-arm reading (F or f) in the dual ordering
phase_2.fuse_element: Belnap join (μ) of the two arms' B4 readings back into the SIXTEEN_3 lattice
phase_2.fuse_result: a single B4 verdict in {N, T, F, B}: N when both arms empty, T when both confirm, F when both refute, B when they conflict
phase_2.failure_reason: FFUSE3 at step 13 has no FSPLIT3 to pair — ill-typed

phase_3.void_description: the 0-element of the regular closed-subset lattice: ∅ — no measurement taken, no DQI channel defined, the uninitialized channel state
phase_3.true_description: T — the DQI input is constructively proven true in the designated ordering; the affirmative evaluation
phase_3.false_description: F — the DQI input is constructively refuted false in the designated ordering; the negative evaluation
phase_3.both_description: B — the dialetheic B4 reading holding T ∧ F simultaneously, e.g. the miracle-paradice of a contradictory DQI output

steps.domain_action: open the trilattice state on ∅ — no DQI channel has yet been instantiated
assert the identity DQI id on ∅ (still ∅) — self-reference, register = 00
a T-arm preparation pass on the T-side of the upcoming fork — register advance to 01 (truth)
anchor the T-arm with the affirmative Belnap evaluation T — register holds T
a corresponding F-arm preparation pass on the F-side of the upcoming fork — register established at 10 (false)
anchor the F-arm with the negative Belnap evaluation F — register holds F
compose the T-arm and F-arm readings sequentially through the DQI monoid operation — registers concatenate into 11
project back through the identity (regular closed-subset) to take stock of the forked state — register is now 11 (both held)
re-establish T at the top of the reunited B4 verdict — register remains 11 (both still live)
re-establish F at the top of the reunited B4 verdict — the contradiction is now explicit
Belnap join (μ) of the two arms — rejoin the fork into a single B4 verdict in {N, T, F, B}
now open a new fork on the B verdict: send B through a refinement channel that splits (B, T) and (B, F)
on the new T-arm, the affirmative reading is B (miraculous)
on the new F-arm, the negative reading is also B (paradice)
Belnap-join the (B, T) and (B, F) arms — both carry B, so rejoin stays at B
compose this B verdict with the previous B4 trace — a stack of two B readings accumulates
attempt a designated-ordering reversal (miracle-max) on the accumulated B — the negation on the SIXTEEN_3 lattice is the central involution
re-check the T-arm after the involution — the involutive negation swaps T ↔ F and t ↔ f, leaving the B verdict invariant
re-check the F-arm after the involution — same invariance
open a third fork to inspect whether the B verdict is actually a superposition or a single point
on the affirmative side, the point remains a single lattice vertex (B)
on the negative side, the point also remains a single lattice vertex (B)
rejoin — the fork does not split the B reading into a genuine superposition, it stays at a single B4 verdict
compose the closed B verification with the DQI evaluation operator δ (the Müller–Aguilera DQI's designated action on regular closed sets)
the DQI operates as an endomorphism of the SIXTEEN_3 lattice, and identity on the verified B vertex is preserved
final affirmative check of the entire DQI — T side of the verdict is consistent
final negative check of the entire DQI — F side of the verdict is also consistent
hold the contradiction in its final state — the B4 verdict is B (paradice), kept live without resolution
freeze the final B4 verdict into a permanent append-only audit record of the DQI evaluation, ROM-style
seal the channel — the entire SIXTEEN_3 lattice is the closed boundary containing this DQI derivation
final self-reference — the IMASM sequence, evaluated over the SIXTEEN_3 state space, returns to its originating lattice vertex with the B4 verdict intact

phase_5.compiler_frontend: the Belnap–Dunn lattice evaluator (the Belnap join and Müller functor restricted to the regular closed-subset lattice of a 2-point deontic algebra)
phase_5.ipc_mechanism: G3-channel composition: the DQI monoid's associative composition (a ∘ b) acts as the inter-process communication primitive between sub-channels of the fork
phase_5.memory_mechanism: the SIXTEEN_3 trilattice itself: the 16-element subset of P({T, F, t, f}) under the three orderings (information ≤k, truth ≤t, validity ≤c) serves as the system's persistent memory substrate
phase_5.scheduler_mechanism: the designated-ordering (≤k) of the SIXTEEN_3 bilattice acts as the scheduler, dispatching fork arms in information order with the miracle-max ≤c precedence
phase_5.alfs_store: the canonical SIXTEEN_3 trilattice (Aguilera–Baez–Mundici / Bou–Rivieccio / similar) — the definitive B4-valued state space that the kernel runs the IMASM token word over

phase_6.cycle_cost: one Belnap-join operation (μ: B4 × B4 → B4) per fork/rejoin cycle, plus one designated-ordering evaluation per arm
phase_6.pre_cycle_state: a regular closed input Ω ∈ RC(2) about to enter a DQI channel; the B4 register is at the identity vertex (N)
phase_6.post_cycle_state: a single B4 verdict in {N, T, F, B} with the full three-ordering information recorded in the audit log (IFIX)
phase_6.delta_s_verdict: ΔS ≈ 0 — every DQI channel is a join-irreversible monotone endomorphism of the SIXTEEN_3 lattice, and the Belnap join is associative and idempotent, so the composition is entropy-conservative
